en: Jose Rizal wrote the novel Noli Me Tangere to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government in the Philippines.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous ancestors over 2,000 years ago.
The Philippine eagle is the largest and rarest eagle in the world and is endemic to the country.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The legislative branch of the Philippine government, called Congress, is responsible for making and repealing laws.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a distinctive two-steps-forward, one-step-back dance.
The T'boli people of South Cotabato weave t'nalak, a traditional cloth made from abaca plant fibers.
Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system where characters represent syllables, used before Spanish colonization.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator for rural areas and founded the first pediatric hospital in Asia.
National Artist Juan Luna painted the Spoliarium, a famous artwork that won a gold medal in Madrid.
Filipino scientist Dr. Ramon Barba invented flower induction technology that allows mango trees to bear fruit year-round.
The traditional value of bayanihan is symbolized by neighbors carrying a nipa hut to a new location.
